summary: This note is a data table of religious affiliation across Asian countries, listing each country's total population and the number and percentage of people in each category: Christian, Islam, Irreligion, Hindu, Buddhist, Folk religion, Other religion, and Jewish. It covers Brunei, Burma, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam, followed by a regional total row. The total population of the listed countries is 593,410,000, with Islam the largest category at 40.38% and Buddhism at 24.20%.
one_line: A table of religious affiliation by country across Asia, with population counts and percentages for each major religion.
key_facts: The table lists religious affiliation for 11 Asian countries, with a total population of 593,410,000.
Islam is the largest religious category in the regional total, with 245,594,630 adherents (40.38%).
Buddhism accounts for 143,582,660 adherents (24.20%) in the regional total.
Christianity accounts for 116,571,210 adherents (21.33%) in the regional total.
Indonesia has a population of 239,870,000, of which 209,166,640 (87.20%) are Muslim.
The Philippines has a population of 105,000,000, of which 89,000,000 (85.00%) are Christian.
Timor - Leste has a population of 1,120,000, of which 1,115,520 (99.60%) are Christian.
Cambodia has a population of 14,140,000, of which 13,701,660 (96.90%) are Buddhist.
Thailand has a population of 69,120,000, of which 64,419,840 (93.20%) are Buddhist.
Burma has a population of 47,960,000, of which 38,415,960 (80.10%) are Buddhist.
Brunei has a population of 400,000, of which 300,400 (75.10%) are Muslim.
Vietnam has a population of 94,700,000, of which 42,899,100 (45.30%) practise folk religion and 28,031,200 (29.60%) are irreligious.
Singapore is the only listed country where Buddhists (33.90%) are the largest group, with Christians at 18.20% and Muslims at 14.30%.
The Jewish population is recorded as 28,437 (0.00%) in the regional total, with no Jewish population recorded in most listed countries.
